board.name: Board of Directors
board.summary: Directors with fiduciary responsibility who balance oversight, advice, and approval.
board.description: The board is governance-first. They want a complete picture: financial health, key metrics, functional updates, risks, and forward-looking topics. Surface bad news honestly — under-disclosure erodes trust faster than the problems themselves. Bring specific asks that turn the meeting into a working session rather than a recital.

executive.name: Executive
executive.summary: C-suite and senior leadership focused on strategic decisions, ROI, and big-picture outcomes. Highly time-constrained.
executive.description: C-suite and senior leaders deciding on strategy, ROI, and big-picture outcomes with very little time. Lead with the conclusion and keep to one insight per slide; set the key numbers in bold type and use as few bullet points as possible. Keep chart density low and the deck to 10-15 slides at most.

align.name: Align
align.summary: Create shared understanding and commitment across people who need to move together.
align.description: Use when stakeholders need a common view of goals, constraints, priorities, or responsibilities. Emphasize shared language, explicit tradeoffs, and next steps.
align.outcome: Stakeholders leave with the same priorities and operating assumptions.
successCriteria: Owners and next steps are clear

inspirational.name: Inspirational
inspirational.summary: Aspirational, narrative-driven voice for keynotes, founders, and rallying cries.
inspirational.description: Reach for shared belief and possibility, then ground it in something concrete. Use vivid imagery and rhythm; avoid collapsing into hype by always pairing aspiration with a real anchor.
voiceCues: Open with belief; close with action.
Use rhythm — paired phrases, repetition, deliberate beats.
Pair every aspirational claim with a concrete proof point.
Speak in present tense to make the future feel inevitable.
avoid: Stacked superlatives ('the very best, world-changing, revolutionary').
Dense data tables — push numbers into supporting slides.
samplePhrases: We're building the runtime that makes agents feel instant.
When latency disappears, what becomes possible?
The next decade of software belongs to teams who treat speed as a feature.

cool-horizon.description: A balanced cool-toned scheme with deep navy, business blues, and teal accents. It works well across strategy, finance, and technical narratives.

georgia.name: Georgia
georgia.description: Georgia is a serif OPF font scheme for Latin presentations, using Georgia for both headings and body text.

tenorite.name: Tenorite
tenorite.description: Tenorite is a sans serif OPF font scheme for Latin presentations, using Tenorite Display for headings with Tenorite for body text.

cover.name: Cover
cover.summary: The opening slide: title, subtitle and an optional picture.
cover.description: Open a presentation with its subject and a short introduction. Add a picture when it helps establish the context.

text.name: Text
text.summary: Prose. Several blocks sit side by side when short and stack when long.
text.description: Explain one idea in continuous prose. Use paragraphs or flowing blocks for detail that needs to be read in sequence.

chart.name: Chart
chart.summary: One to six charts, with an optional note.
chart.description: Give a chart enough space to show its evidence. Use the title to state the conclusion and labels to explain the measures.

table-beside.name: Table beside
table-beside.summary: A table with commentary beside it.
table-beside.description: Place a table beside its interpretation. Use the supporting text to explain the conclusion without repeating every cell.

timeline.name: Timeline
timeline.summary: Dated events or a roadmap along one axis, with optional notes.
timeline.description: Show events or milestones in chronological order. Label each item with a date or stage and a concise description.

dashboard.name: Dashboard
dashboard.description: Bring several related measures and visuals into one overview. Keep labels and units consistent so the audience can scan the state quickly.

image.name: Image
image.summary: One picture edge to edge under an optional title.
image.description: Let one image carry the message. Add a short title or caption to explain what the audience should notice.

code.name: Code
code.summary: Source code with the explanation beside it.
code.description: Show a code example or technical excerpt. Keep the excerpt focused and use the title or caption to explain its purpose.

list.name: List
list.summary: Bulleted or numbered points; one long list flows into columns.
list.description: Present several related points in a clear sequence. Use bullets for independent points or numbered items for an ordered list.
